Phase 1 — v1.0

Automated Binance ETL Pipeline

A robust ETL pipeline ingesting crypto market data from the Binance API, transforming with Pandas, and landing in Amazon S3 as date-partitioned Parquet files — orchestrated with Apache Airflow on a Dockerized EC2 instance.

Binance API → Python → Pandas → S3 Parquet
Orch: Airflow DAGs (hourly) · Infra: Docker + EC2
Incremental loads with timestamp tracking
Config-driven column renaming & strict data typing
Date-partitioned Parquet via fastparquet
CeleryExecutor + PostgreSQL + Redis backend
PythonAirflowAWS S3PandasDockerEC2
↗ View repository

Phase 2 — v2.0 · Production-Ready

Dual-Sink Pipeline with ClickHouse & CI/CD

Evolved the pipeline into a production-ready system with a real-time analytics engine, infrastructure observability, and fully automated zero-downtime deployments — without touching the core ETL logic.

Airflow → S3 (archive) + ClickHouse NEW
Monitor: Grafana · Deploy: GitHub Actions NEW
Dual-sink: S3 + ClickHouse simultaneously
Sub-second GROUP BY queries on columnar storage
Grafana monitors latency, memory & CPU live
Rolling restart + /health check — zero downtime

Medallion Architecture with dbt + Dagster

// 05 — about

About Me

I'm Tin, a data engineer based in Thailand with 3+ years of experience building production-grade data infrastructure. I've worked across crypto (Bitazza), food-tech (Freshket), consulting (PwC), and insurance (FWD).

My day-to-day involves designing pipelines that are reliable, observable, and easy to extend — whether that's a Pub/Sub stream into BigQuery, a dbt medallion model in ClickHouse, or a zero-downtime CI/CD deploy via GitHub Actions.

I believe clean architecture pays off the moment you want to extend it. The ETL foundation I built for my personal project required almost zero changes when scaling to a full medallion architecture.

Currently open to data engineering roles, pipeline architecture projects, and consulting opportunities.
